definition_zh: 方言；土语；用语
definition_en: a form of a language spoken in one area or by one group of people
core_image: 同一条街两头的人，用不同腔调说同一个词
scene: 集市上卖菜的老人把「土豆」说成另一个音，年轻人听不太懂。The dialect spoken in the valley has its own words for rain.
sceneCN: 这里 dialect 指「方言」（第 1 个义项：某一地区通行的语言变体）；句意是山谷里说的方言有自己一套表示雨的词。

senses.title: A regional form of a language
senses.definition: a form of a language spoken in one particular area
senses.definitionCN: 在某一特定地区通行的一种语言形式
senses.example: The dialect spoken in the valley has its own words for rain.
senses.exampleCN: 山谷里说的方言有自己一套表示雨的词。
senses.why: Every valley keeps its own small vocabulary for weather.
senses.whyCN: 每个山谷都为天气留着自己的一小套词。

senses.title: A group's way of speaking
senses.definition: the speech of a social group or trade rather than a whole region
senses.definitionCN: 某一社会群体或行业而非整个地区所说的语言
senses.example: The dock workers had a dialect full of sea words.
senses.exampleCN: 码头工人有一种满是海上词汇的土语。
senses.why: A trade grows its own words the way a garden grows its own weeds.
senses.whyCN: 一个行业长出自己的词，就像园子长出自己的草。

senses.title: A particular style of speech
senses.definition: a special way of speaking used by a group or in a piece of writing
senses.definitionCN: 某个群体或某篇作品里使用的特别说法
senses.example: The poem is written in the dialect of the streets.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗用的是街头那套用语。
senses.why: A style of speech is a costume a text can wear.
senses.whyCN: 一种说话方式，是文字可以穿上的戏服。

intro.en: Dialect comes from Greek dialektos, a conversation or the speech of a region, from dialegesthai, to talk with someone.
intro.cn: dialect 来自希腊语 dialektos（交谈、某地区的说话方式），源自动词 dialegesthai（与人交谈）。

items.en: Dialegesthai meant to talk something through with another person.
items.cn: dialegesthai 指与另一个人把话说透。

items.en: Dialektos named the speech of a particular place or group.
items.cn: dialektos 指某个地方或群体特有的说话方式。

items.en: Latin dialectus kept the sense of a local form of Greek.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dialectus 保留了「希腊语的地方变体」这一意思。

items.en: English dialect was used for regional forms of any language.
items.cn: 英语 dialect 用来指任何语言的地方变体。

items.en: Linguists now treat dialects as full systems, not errors.
items.cn: 如今语言学家把方言看作完整系统，而不是错误。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dia- opening, and the meaning group names accents, local speech and languages.
note.cn: 形近组共用 dia- 开头，近义组则指口音、本地话与语言。

entries.definition: belonging to a local form of speech
entries.definitionCN: 属于地方说话形式的

entries.definition: a conversation between people
entries.definitionCN: 人与人之间的交谈

entries.definition: reasoning through opposing ideas
entries.definitionCN: 通过对立观点推进的推理

entries.definition: the way a group pronounces words
entries.definitionCN: 一群人说词的发音方式

entries.definition: the everyday speech of ordinary people
entries.definitionCN: 普通人日常说的话

entries.definition: a system of words used by a people
entries.definitionCN: 一个民族使用的词语系统

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with two accents on one street and end with a poem wearing the speech of the street.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从同一条街上的两种腔调开始，落到一首穿着街头用语的诗。

normal.en: Dialect began as the word for conversation, not for error.
normal.cn: dialect 最初是「交谈」的意思，并不是「错误」。

normal.en: A valley can put its own name on the rain.
normal.cn: 一个山谷，能给雨起自己的名字。

normal.en: Every trade carries a small dictionary in its pocket.
normal.cn: 每个行业的口袋里都装着一本小词典。

normal.en: An accent is how it sounds; a dialect is what it says.
normal.cn: 口音是听起来怎样，方言是说了些什么。

normal.en: Two villages, one language, and a fence of words between them.
normal.cn: 两个村子，一种语言，中间隔着一道词的篱笆。

abstract.en: Picture two old men saying one word differently.
abstract.cn: 想象两位老人把同一个词说成两个样。

abstract.en: Picture a market stall with a hand-written sign.
abstract.cn: 想象一个摊位上挂着块手写的牌子。

abstract.en: Picture a poem printed with odd spellings.
abstract.cn: 想象一首诗，印着些奇怪的拼法。

examples.en: The dialect spoken in the valley has its own words for rain.
examples.cn: 山谷里说的方言有自己一套表示雨的词。

examples.en: The dock workers had a dialect full of sea words.
examples.cn: 码头工人有一种满是海上词汇的土语。

examples.en: The poem is written in the dialect of the streets.
examples.cn: 这首诗用的是街头那套用语。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dialect 记成「带个来客」：dia 是穿过，lect 是说，一个地方的人穿过来说的话，就是方言。

root: 来自希腊语 dialektos，源自动词 dialegesthai（交谈），本义是与人把话说透。经拉丁语进入英语后，专指某一地区或群体所说的语言变体，现代语言学把它看作完整系统而非错误说法。

sensesIntro.en: From the speech of one valley, to the private words of a trade, to a style a poem can wear.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个山谷的说话方式，到一个行业的私房词，再到一首诗能穿上的腔调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one word pronounced two ways at the two ends of a street.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个词，在一条街的两头有两种读法。

branches.en: The first sense is the speech of one piece of land.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是一片土地上的人说的话。

branches.en: The second sense follows a trade instead of a place.
branches.cn: 第二个义项跟着一个行业走，而不是跟着地方走。

branches.en: The third sense is that speech borrowed into writing.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是那种话被借进了文字里。

branches.en: A region and a workshop both keep their own small vocabulary.
branches.cn: 一个地区与一个作坊，都守着自己的一小套词。

branches.en: A way of speaking can become a style on the page.
branches.cn: 一种说话方式，能变成纸面上的一种风格。

intro.en: Dialect has a family built on conversation and on the study of local speech.
intro.cn: dialect 有一族词，建在交谈与对地方话的研究上。

latinIntro.en: The Greek base means to talk something through, and the family grew around regional speech.
latinIntro.cn: 它的希腊词基意为把事情谈透，这一族词围绕地方话生长。

items.example: This dialect is hard to follow.

items.exampleCN: 这两种形式在方言上不同。
这位方言学家把边界标在地图上。

items.example: The text was dialectalized on purpose.
items.exampleCN: 这段文字被有意加上了方言色彩。
这场争论沿着一种辩证方式推进。

definition_zh: 对话；对白；（正式）磋商；对话体作品
definition_en: a conversation between two or more people, especially one that exchanges ideas
core_image: 两束声音穿过中间的空隙，来回碰撞，谁也不压住谁
scene: 两国代表在长桌两侧轮流发言，记者在报道中写道：The dialogue resumed after months of silence.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「双方或多方之间的对话」（第 1 个义项：两人以上交流看法）；句意为沉默数月之后对话重新开始。

pos.zh: 对话；对白；正式磋商；对话体作品
（较少用）进行对话；用对话表达

senses.title: Conversation between two or more people
senses.titleCN: 两人或多人之间的对话
senses.definition: a spoken exchange in which two or more people take turns
senses.definitionCN: 两人或多人轮流发言的口头交流
senses.example: The film's dialogue sounds natural and unforced.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的对白听起来自然、不做作。
senses.why: The Greek root joins 'between' with 'speech', so the word begins as speech that passes between parties.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词根把「之间」与「言语」结合，因此这个词一开始就是在各方之间穿行的言语。

senses.title: An exchange of views or negotiation
senses.definition: organized discussion between parties who may disagree, aimed at mutual understanding
senses.definitionCN: 可能存在分歧的各方之间有组织的讨论，旨在相互理解
senses.example: The two sides opened a dialogue on water rights.
senses.exampleCN: 双方就水权开启了对话。
senses.why: When the parties are institutions, the between-ness becomes the point: the talk is a channel between positions.
senses.whyCN: 当各方是机构时，「之间」本身成了重点：谈话是立场之间的通道。

senses.title: A literary form
senses.definition: a work written as a conversation, especially a philosophical or instructive one
senses.definitionCN: 以谈话形式写成的作品，尤其是哲学或教导性的作品
senses.example: Plato wrote philosophy as dialogue.
senses.exampleCN: 柏拉图以对话体写作哲学。
senses.why: The form preserves the back-and-forth of speech instead of flattening it into a single voice.
senses.whyCN: 这种体裁保留言语的来回往复，而不是把它压平成单一声音。

senses.title: Scripted speech in film or theatre
senses.definition: the lines spoken by characters in a script, film or play
senses.definitionCN: 剧本、电影或戏剧中人物说出的台词
senses.example: The dialogue was improvised on set.
senses.exampleCN: 这些对白是在片场即兴的。
senses.why: Performance writes down the between-speech and calls the written version dialogue.
senses.whyCN: 表演把「之间的言语」写下来，并把写成的版本称为对白。

senses.title: A philosophical method
senses.definition: a method of inquiry that proceeds through questions and answers rather than a lecture
senses.definitionCN: 通过问答而不是讲授推进的探究方法
senses.example: Socratic dialogue proceeds by questions rather than assertions.
senses.exampleCN: 苏格拉底式对话靠提问而不是断言推进。
senses.why: Philosophy turned the exchange into a method, where each answer opens the next question.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把这种交流变成方法，每个回答都打开下一个问题。

senses.title: Internal dialogue
senses.definition: the conversation a person holds with themselves in thought
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在思想中与自己的交谈
senses.example: She kept a silent dialogue with herself before the speech.
senses.exampleCN: 演讲前她与自己进行了一场无声的对话。
senses.why: The between-ness can be internal: one mind takes both parts of the exchange.
senses.whyCN: 「之间」可以转向内部：一个心灵承担交流的双方。

senses.title: A dialog box in computing
senses.definition: a small window that asks the user for information or a decision
senses.definitionCN: 向用户索取信息或要求作出决定的小窗口
senses.example: A dialog box asked for the password.
senses.exampleCN: 一个对话框要求输入密码。
senses.why: The interface borrows the word because the box conducts a short exchange with the user.
senses.whyCN: 界面借用这个词，因为这个框与用户进行一段简短交流。

senses.title: Classroom dialogue
senses.definition: collaborative talk among students and teachers used as a tool for learning
senses.definitionCN: 师生之间作为学习工具的合作性谈话
senses.example: Classroom dialogue improves reasoning more than lecturing does.
senses.exampleCN: 课堂对话比讲授更能改善推理。
senses.why: Education treats talk as a way of thinking together, so the exchange becomes a learning method.
senses.whyCN: 教育把谈话当作共同思考的方式，因此交流成为学习方法。

intro.en: Dialogue comes through Latin and French from Greek dialogos, built on dia- 'through, between' and logos 'word, speech, reason'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: dialogue 经拉丁语与法语来自希腊语 dialogos，由希腊语表示「穿过、之间」的前缀与 logos「词、言语、理性」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Logos meant 'word, speech, account, reason'. Its deeper origin is connected with a verb meaning 'to gather or say', but the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: logos 意为「词、言语、叙述、理性」。其更深来源与一个表示「收集、说」的动词有关，但重构并不确定。

items.en: Dia- meant 'through, across, between', and in dialogos it marked speech passing between parties.
items.cn: 这个希腊前缀意为「穿过、横过、之间」，在 dialogos 中标记在各方之间穿行的言语。

items.en: Dialogos named a conversation or a philosophical exchange; Plato made it the name of a literary form.
items.cn: dialogos 指谈话或哲学交流；柏拉图使它成为一种文学体裁的名称。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word as dialogus and passed it to medieval and modern European languages.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊词成为 dialogus，并把它传给中世纪与现代欧洲语言。

items.en: English dialogue appears in the thirteenth century through French; the American spelling dialog became common in computing.
items.cn: 英语 dialogue 在十三世纪经法语出现；美式拼写 dialog 在计算领域变得常见。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact pre-Greek origin of logos is debated, and the first English citation of the literary sense is not fixed; proposed roots are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：logos 在希腊语之前的来源有争议，文学义的最早英语书证也没有定论；提出的词根属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the spelling variant and words built with different prefixes from the same speech root; group two holds near synonyms for an exchange of talk.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写变体，以及与同一「言语」词根搭配不同前缀的词；第二组是表示交谈的近义词。

entries.definition: The American spelling of the same word, now standard for the computing window and common in US fiction.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的美式拼写，现为计算机窗口的标准写法，也常用于美国小说。

entries.definition: The second part comes from a Greek verb meaning 'to speak' in a different root line; a dialect is a regional variety, not a conversation.
entries.definitionCN: 后半部分来自另一条词根线上表示「说话」的希腊动词；方言是地区变体，不是对话。

entries.definition: A play or scene for exactly two speakers; dialogue has no such numerical limit.
entries.definitionCN: 为恰好两个说话人写的戏剧或场景；dialogue 没有这种人数限制。

entries.definition: It uses a prefix meaning 'one' with the same speech root, so it names a long speech by a single voice.
entries.definitionCN: 用表示「一」的前缀与同一言语词根组合，命名单一声音的长篇发言。

entries.definition: The everyday word for informal talk; dialogue often implies an exchange between sides or a literary form.
entries.definitionCN: 指非正式谈话的日常用词；dialogue 常暗示各方之间的交流或文学形式。

entries.definition: A talk organized around a topic or decision; dialogue stresses the exchange between voices.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕主题或决定组织的谈话；dialogue 强调声音之间的交流。

entries.definition: Formal negotiations between parties; dialogue can be broader and need not aim at a settlement.
entries.definitionCN: 各方之间的正式谈判；dialogue 可以更宽，也不必以达成协议为目标。

entries.definition: A general word for giving and receiving; dialogue is specifically an exchange of speech.
entries.definitionCN: 指给予与接受的宽泛词；dialogue 特指言语的交换。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the 'between' prefix, the speech root, the literary form and the modern window.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示「之间」的前缀、「言语」词根、文学形式与现代窗口。

normal.en: The prefix means 'between', the root means 'speech', so dialogue is speech passing between people.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「之间」，词根意为「言语」，因此对话就是在人与人之间穿行的言语。

normal.en: Prefix contrast: one voice gives a monologue, two voices a duologue, many voices a dialogue.
normal.cn: 前缀对比：一个声音是独白，两个声音是双人对话，多个声音是对话。

normal.en: Plato turned the exchange into a literary form that still bears the name.
normal.cn: 柏拉图把这种交流变成一种至今仍用此名的文学体裁。

normal.en: Film and theatre call the written talk of characters dialogue.
normal.cn: 电影与戏剧把人物写下来的谈话称为对白。

normal.en: Computing uses the shorter American spelling for a dialog box.
normal.cn: 计算领域用较短的美式拼写指对话框。

abstract.en: Picture two voices meeting in the empty space between two chairs.
abstract.cn: 想象两个声音在两张椅子之间的空处相遇。

abstract.en: Picture a question and an answer holding hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一个问题与一个回答手拉着手。

abstract.en: Picture a small window that asks you one question before it opens.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小窗口在打开之前先问你一个问题。

examples.en: The novel is mostly dialogue, with very little description.
examples.cn: 这部小说大部分是对白，描写很少。

examples.en: The union and the management agreed to resume dialogue.
examples.cn: 工会与管理层同意恢复对话。

examples.en: A dialogue box appeared asking whether to save the file.
examples.cn: 弹出一个对话框，询问是否保存文件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「两者之间」加「说话」——两边来回说 → 对话、对白

root: 希腊语 dialogos = 表示「穿过、之间」的前缀 + logos「词、言语、理性」，经拉丁语 dialogus 与法语进入英语。logos 的更早来源有争议，相关词根为重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow speech between parties: a general exchange, formal talks, a literary form, a script, a philosophical method, inner talk, a computer window and classroom learning.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿「各方之间的言语」展开：一般交流、正式磋商、文学体裁、脚本、哲学方法、内心交谈、计算机窗口与课堂学习。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two streams of speech cross the space between two parties.
core.cn: 核心意象：两股言语穿过两方之间的空间。

branches.en: EXCHANGE: ordinary turn-taking and classroom talk both use speech as a shared tool.
branches.cn: 交流：日常轮流发言与课堂谈话都把言语当作共享工具。

branches.en: BETWEEN SIDES: the parties may disagree, and the talk is the channel between their positions.
branches.cn: 各方之间：各方可能存在分歧，谈话是立场之间的通道。

branches.en: FORM AND METHOD: a written dialogue preserves turn-taking, and a philosophical dialogue turns it into inquiry.
branches.cn: 形式与方法：书面对话保留轮流往复，哲学对话把它变成探究。

branches.en: SCRIPT: performance writes the exchange down as lines for characters.
branches.cn: 脚本：表演把交流写成人物的台词。

branches.en: INNER AND MACHINE: one mind can take both parts, and a window can take the other part for a machine.
branches.cn: 内心与机器：一个心灵可以承担双方，一个窗口也可以替机器承担另一方。

intro.en: Dialogue is a Greek compound of 'between' and 'speech', and the same pieces build monologue, duologue and the adjective of dialogic form.
intro.cn: dialogue 是希腊语中「之间」与「言语」的合成词，同样的部件还构成独白、双人对话与对话形式的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Greek dia- and logos formed dialogos, which Latin borrowed as dialogus; English adds adjective and adverb suffixes to build the family.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语表示「穿过、之间」的前缀与 logos 构成 dialogos，拉丁语借入为 dialogus；英语再加形容词与副词后缀构成词族。

items.example: The prefix marks speech crossing between parties.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记在各方之间穿行的言语。

items.example: The root names speech and its rational order.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名言语及其理性秩序。

items.example: The Greek word named an exchange of speeches.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊词命名言语的交换。

items.example: Latin kept the word for learned conversation.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语保留这个词指有学问的交谈。

items.example: The play opens with a long dialogue.
items.exampleCN: 这部戏以一段长对白开场。

items.example: The novel has a dialogic structure.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说具有对话式结构。

items.example: The class used a dialogical approach.
items.exampleCN: 这门课采用对话式方法。

items.example: The actor delivered a long monologue.
items.exampleCN: 演员说了一段长长的独白。

items.example: The second act is a duologue.
items.exampleCN: 第二幕是一段双人对话。

items.meaning: a regional variety of a language
items.example: The dialect differs from the standard in its vowels.
items.exampleCN: 这种方言在元音上与标准语不同。

definition_zh: 直径；直径长度；口径
definition_en: a straight line across a circle through its centre, or the length of that line
core_image: 一根细线从圆的一边穿过圆心拉到另一边
scene: 木匠把圆桌翻过来，用卷尺从一边量到另一边，尺子正好过中心。The diameter of the table is one metre.
sceneCN: 这里 diameter 指「直径」（第 1 个义项：穿过圆心、两端落在圆上的线段）；句意是这张桌子的直径是一米。

senses.title: A line across a circle
senses.definition: a straight line that passes through the centre of a circle and touches both sides
senses.definitionCN: 穿过圆心、两端都落在圆上的直线
senses.example: The diameter of the table is one metre.
senses.exampleCN: 这张桌子的直径是一米。
senses.why: The longest straight path through a round thing must pass its centre.
senses.whyCN: 穿过一个圆东西的最长直线，必然经过它的中心。

senses.title: The length measured that way
senses.definition: the length of such a line, used as a measure of how wide a round thing is
senses.definitionCN: 这条线的长度，用来衡量圆形物体有多宽
senses.example: The circle has a diameter of ten centimetres.

definition_zh: 独裁者；专政者；古罗马独裁官；专横的人；口述者
definition_en: a ruler who holds absolute power, especially one who seizes it and rules without checks
core_image: 一个站在高台上的人，台下的人排队递交请愿，台上只有一支笔和一个印章
scene: 广场广播里，一个人的声音宣布取消原定的投票，人群在台下沉默。The dictator cancelled the vote and ruled by decree for a decade.
sceneCN: 广场广播里，一个人的声音宣布取消原定的投票，人群在台下沉默；句中这个词指「掌握绝对权力、尤其以夺取方式取得政权的统治者」（第 1 个义项：不受制衡、独自掌握国家最高权力的人）。句意为这个独裁者取消投票，并以法令统治了十年。可辨识物件：广播喇叭、取消的投票牌、高台、沉默的人群。

senses.title: A ruler with absolute power
senses.titleCN: 掌握绝对权力的统治者
senses.definition: a person who holds the highest power of a state and cannot be removed by any independent body
senses.definitionCN: 掌握国家最高权力、任何独立机构都无法将其免职的人
senses.example: The dictator cancelled the vote and ruled by decree for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这个独裁者取消投票，并以法令统治了十年。
senses.why: Latin dictator named the holder of an emergency office who spoke with final authority, and English kept the person while widening the power.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 dictator 指在紧急状态下以最终权威发令的官员，英语保留了这个指人的词，同时扩大了权力范围。

senses.title: One who seized power
senses.titleCN: 以夺取方式取得权力的人
senses.definition: a ruler who took office by force or by cancelling elections rather than by a lawful contest
senses.definitionCN: 靠武力或取消选举而非合法竞争取得职位的人
senses.example: The general became dictator after the coup.
senses.exampleCN: 政变之后，这位将军成了独裁者。
senses.why: The modern word is defined less by the office than by how it was obtained, so seizure is part of its everyday meaning.
senses.whyCN: 现代词义与其说由职位界定，不如说由取得方式界定，因此「夺取」成了它日常含义的一部分。

senses.title: The Roman emergency magistrate
senses.definition: in ancient Rome, a magistrate appointed for a limited term with sweeping powers in an emergency
senses.definitionCN: 古罗马在紧急状态下任命、任期有限却权力广泛的官员
senses.example: The Senate appointed a dictator to meet the invasion.
senses.exampleCN: 元老院任命了一位独裁官来应对入侵。
senses.why: The Roman office was legal and temporary, a fact that makes the modern word's tone look like a reversal.
senses.whyCN: 罗马的职位合法且临时，这一事实使现代词义的语气看起来像一次反转。

senses.title: A domineering person in a group
senses.definition: a member of a team, office or family who insists on deciding everything
senses.definitionCN: 在团队、办公室或家庭里坚持决定一切的人
senses.example: The office manager acted like a dictator.
senses.exampleCN: 这位办公室主管行事像个独裁者。
senses.why: Unchecked personal power looks the same at any scale, so the political person-word is borrowed for small tyrants.
senses.whyCN: 不受制约的个人权力在任何尺度上看起来都一样，因此这个政治指人词被借来描述小范围的专横者。

senses.title: Leader of an authoritarian state or party
senses.titleCN: 威权国家或政党的领袖
senses.definition: the head of a party or state who controls the police, the press and the courts
senses.definitionCN: 控制警察、新闻与法院的政党或国家领袖
senses.example: The party's dictator controlled the police.
senses.exampleCN: 这个政党的独裁者控制着警察。
senses.why: When a party rather than a person holds power, the person at the top still carries the old title.
senses.whyCN: 当掌权者是政党而非个人时，最高处的那个人仍沿用旧称号。

senses.title: One who dictates text
senses.definition: in older usage, a person who reads words aloud for others to write down
senses.definitionCN: 较早的用法中指朗读词句、让旁人记录的人
senses.example: In the old schoolroom, the dictator read while pupils wrote.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧式教室里，口述者朗读，学生记录。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the plain one: a person who dictates words. The political sense grew out of the authority of the speaking voice.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是朴素的那个：口述词句的人。政治义从言说声音的权威中生长出来。

senses.title: The power behind a government
senses.titleCN: 政府背后的实际掌权者
senses.definition: a person who holds real power while a figurehead occupies the official post
senses.definitionCN: 名义职位由傀儡占据、实际权力归其所有之人
senses.example: The elected president was a figurehead; the real dictator sat in the shadows.
senses.exampleCN: 当选总统只是名义元首；真正的独裁者坐在幕后。
senses.why: Power without a title is still dictatorship, so the word follows the control rather than the office.
senses.whyCN: 没有头衔的权力仍是独裁，因此这个词跟随控制权，而非职位。

senses.title: A leader who dictates terms to others
senses.titleCN: 向他人强加条件的领导者
senses.definition: a leader who imposes conditions on other states or groups without negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 不经协商就向他国或他群体强加条件的领导者
senses.example: The dictator imposed terms on his neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 这位独裁者向邻国强加条件。
senses.why: The verb 'to dictate' survives inside the person-word, and imposing terms is the verb's plainest modern use.
senses.whyCN: 「口述、规定」的动词义仍活在这个指人词内部，而强加条件正是该动词最朴素的现代用法。

intro.en: Dictator is Latin for the holder of an emergency office, from dictare 'to say repeatedly, prescribe'. English took the word in the sixteenth century for the Roman magistrate, and the modern sense of an absolute ruler hardened in the nineteenth and twentieth.
intro.cn: dictator 是拉丁语中紧急状态官职的称呼，出自 dictare「反复说、规定」。英语在十六世纪借入此词指罗马官员，而「绝对统治者」的现代义在十九、二十世纪固定下来。

items.en: Dicere meant 'to say, to speak'. Its older Indo-European root is reconstructed rather than recorded, so any form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: dicere 意为「说、讲」。它更早的印欧词根是重构的，而非有记录的，因此为它提出的任何形式都是重构形式。

items.en: Dictare, a frequentative of dicere, meant 'to say repeatedly, to dictate, to prescribe'. Repetition turned speech into an order.
items.cn: dictare 是 dicere 的反复形式，意为「反复说、口述、规定」。反复使言说变成命令。

items.en: The Roman dictator was appointed in emergencies for a fixed short term and held sweeping but temporary powers. The title is generally thought to refer to the consul's naming him aloud, though that explanation is not certain.
items.cn: 罗马独裁官在紧急状态下被任命，任期固定且很短，权力广泛但属临时。这个称号一般认为是因执政官当众口述其名而来，但这一解释并非定论。

items.en: English dictator first named the Roman magistrate and then any absolute ruler. Dates are approximate, and the shift between the two senses was gradual.
items.cn: 英语 dictator 先指罗马官员，后指任何绝对统治者。年代为约数，两种词义之间的转变是渐进的。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word fixed to rulers who seize or hold power without checks, especially military leaders and party chiefs.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个词固定指夺取或掌握权力且不受制衡的统治者，尤其指军事领袖与政党首脑。

items.en: The twentieth century applied the word to bosses, coaches and parents, and to powers behind elected governments. Source uncertain (first date): the earliest figurative citation is not fixed.
items.cn: 二十世纪把这个词用于上司、教练与家长，也用于民选政府背后的势力。首见年代不确定：最早的比喻书证并无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin dictare family that differ only in ending; group two holds names for other kinds of unchecked ruler.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁 dictare 词族、仅词尾不同的词；第二组是其他不受制约统治者的称呼。

entries.definition: The regime or period, not the person. One overthrows a dictator and ends a dictatorship.
entries.definitionCN: 指政权或时期，而非个人。人推翻独裁者，结束独裁统治。

entries.definition: Describing a ruler or manner as unchecked and bossy; it can modify a decision as well as a person.
entries.definitionCN: 描述统治者或作风不受制约、专横；它可修饰决定，也可修饰人。

entries.definition: To say words for writing, or to impose terms. The verb preserves the speaking sense that the noun has almost lost.
entries.definitionCN: 指口述让人记录，或强加条件。动词保留了名词几乎已失去的言说义。

entries.definition: The act of writing down spoken words, or the classroom task based on it; it shares the root but names no ruler.
entries.definitionCN: 指把口述内容写下来的行为，或据此设置的课堂练习；它同根，却不指任何统治者。

entries.definition: From Greek dēmagōgos 'leader of the people', built on 'lead', not 'say'. A demagogue stirs a crowd but need not hold absolute power.
entries.definitionCN: 出自希腊 dēmagōgos「民众的领袖」，基础是「引导」而非「说」。煽动者搅动人群，却未必掌握绝对权力。

entries.definition: A ruler who uses power unjustly and cruelly; the word judges the rule, while dictator describes how power is held.
entries.definitionCN: 不义而残酷地行使权力的统治者；这个词评判统治，而 dictator 描述权力如何被掌握。

entries.definition: A ruler who holds authority alone, often by inherited right; a dictator typically seizes power instead.
entries.definitionCN: 独自掌握权威的统治者，常凭继承权；独裁者则通常靠夺取权力。

entries.definition: A ruler whose word is law and whose choices follow his mood; the word stresses arbitrariness.
entries.definitionCN: 一句话就是法律、选择随心情而定的统治者；这个词强调任意性。

entries.definition: An informal term for a leader who rules by force and personality; it describes the style rather than the constitution.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中指靠武力与个人魅力统治的领袖；它描述风格，而非宪制。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin verb, a real Roman office and a real family of English forms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、真实的罗马官职与真实的英语词族。

normal.en: Dictate, dictator, dictatorship: speaking with authority becomes a person, then a system.
normal.cn: dictate、dictator、dictatorship：带权威的言说变成一个人，再变成一套制度。

normal.en: The family runs dictate, dictation, dictator, dictatorial, dictatorship.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 dictate、dictation、dictator、dictatorial、dictatorship。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: a military dictator, overthrow the dictator, a puppet dictator.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：军事独裁者、推翻独裁者、傀儡独裁者。

normal.en: The Roman dictator was legal and temporary, unlike the modern figure.
normal.cn: 罗马独裁官合法且临时，与现代人物不同。

normal.en: The word can name a general, a party chief, a boss or a coach, because unchecked power has no fixed size.
normal.cn: 这个词可指将军、政党首脑、上司或教练，因为不受制约的权力没有固定尺度。

abstract.en: Picture one hand holding both a pen and a seal.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手同时握着笔与印章。

abstract.en: Picture a microphone that no one else is allowed to touch.
abstract.cn: 想象一支不许别人碰的话筒。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow standing behind an empty official chair.
abstract.cn: 想象一道影子站在一把空着的正式椅子后面。

examples.en: The dictator banned every party but his own.
examples.cn: 这位独裁者取缔了除自己政党之外的所有政党。

examples.en: Ancient writers described the dictator's six-month term.
examples.cn: 古代作家记述了独裁官六个月的任期。

examples.en: The team's captain behaved like a dictator on the field.
examples.cn: 这支球队的队长在球场上行事像个独裁者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「口述」加「人」：一个人说了算；这属构词说明，并非谐音联想

root: 拉丁 dicere「说」（更早印欧词根为重构形式）→ dictare「反复说、口述、规定」→ dictator（罗马临时独裁官，称号来源一般认为是当众口述其名，但非定论）→ 英语 dictator（十六世纪）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one figure from a Roman office to a shadow behind a chair: the absolute ruler, the man who seized power, the ancient magistrate, the office bully, the party chief, the reader of texts, the power behind a figurehead and the leader who dictates terms.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一个人物从罗马官职走到椅后的影子：绝对统治者、夺权者、古代官员、办公室里的专横者、政党首脑、朗读文本者、傀儡背后的实权者，以及强加条件的领袖。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure on a raised platform holding a pen and a seal while a queue of petitioners waits below.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个站在高台上的人手里握着笔与印章，台下排着递交请愿的人。

branches.en: Absolute power and the way it was taken are one story: the modern word begins with the seizure.
branches.cn: 绝对权力与取得方式是一个故事：现代词义从夺取开始。

branches.en: The Roman office and the classroom reader share the oldest layer, where the title meant the speaking authority.
branches.cn: 罗马官职与课堂朗读者共享最古老的一层，那里的称号指言说的权威。

branches.en: A boss reproduces the whole structure in one room, because unchecked power needs no constitution.
branches.cn: 一个上司就能在一间屋子里复制整套结构，因为不受制约的权力不需要宪法。

branches.en: The party chief and the shadow behind the chair are the same power with and without a title.
branches.cn: 政党首脑与椅后的影子，是同一权力有头衔与无头衔的两种样子。

branches.en: Dictating terms abroad is the old verb of speech turned into foreign policy.
branches.cn: 对外强加条件，是把古老的言说动词变成外交政策。

intro.en: Dictator is a Latin person-noun built on the verb for repeated speech, and the same family supplies the system, the adjective and the classroom task.
intro.cn: dictator 是建立在「反复言说」动词上的拉丁指人名词，同一词族还提供制度名、形容词与课堂任务名。

latinIntro.en: Latin dicere and dictare supply the root, and dictator supplies the person; the deeper Indo-European root of dicere is reconstructed rather than attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 dicere 与 dictare 提供词根，dictator 提供指人的词；dicere 更早的印欧词根是重构的，而非有书证的。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根指朴素的言说。
反复言说赋予说话者权威。

items.meaning: one who dictates; the Roman magistrate
items.example: The person-noun carries both the title and the office.
items.exampleCN: 这个指人的名词同时承载称号与职位。

items.example: The abstract noun names the post itself.
The agent suffix turns the verb into a person.
items.exampleCN: 施事后缀把动词变成指人的词。

items.meaning: to say for writing; to impose
items.example: English kept the verb beside the borrowed person-noun.
items.exampleCN: 英语在借入指人名词之外保留了动词。

items.example: The native suffix turns the person into a system.
items.exampleCN: 本族后缀把个人变成制度。

items.example: The adjective describes the manner as well as the office.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词既描述作风，也描述职位。

items.meaning: the act of dictating; a writing exercise
items.example: The old speaking sense survives in a school task.
items.exampleCN: 古老的言说义以学校任务的形式留存。

definition_zh: adj. 独裁的；专断的；爱发号施令的；不容争辩的
definition_en: of a ruler or manner that holds total power and expects orders to be obeyed without question
core_image: 会议室里一个人把方案拍在桌上，其他人不许开口；家里遥控器永远在同一个人手里
scene: 他的管理方式很专断。His management style is dictatorial.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：dictatorial 指专断的、独裁的；句意是他的管理方式很专断。

pos.zh: 独裁的；专断的；爱发号施令的

senses.title: Ruling with absolute power
senses.definition: of a government or ruler that holds total power without checks
senses.definitionCN: （政府或统治者）掌握不受制衡的全部权力
senses.example: The country fell under dictatorial rule.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家落入独裁统治。
senses.why: One hand resting on every switch in a control room.
senses.whyCN: 控制室里一只手按在所有开关上。

senses.title: Bossy in everyday dealings
senses.definition: telling people what to do in an overbearing way
senses.definitionCN: 以盛气凌人的方式指挥别人
senses.example: His management style is dictatorial.
senses.exampleCN: 他的管理方式很专断。
senses.why: A plan slammed on a table while others stay silent.
senses.whyCN: 一份方案被拍在桌上，其他人沉默。

senses.title: Allowing no argument
senses.definition: expecting orders to be obeyed without question
senses.definitionCN: 要求命令被无条件服从
senses.example: She resented his dictatorial tone.
senses.exampleCN: 她反感他那不容争辩的语气。
senses.why: A raised finger stopping a raised hand.
senses.whyCN: 一根竖起的手指压住另一只举起的手。

intro.en: Dictatorial comes from Latin dictatorius, from dictator, one who dictates, from dictare, to say repeatedly, from dicere, to say.
intro.cn: dictatorial 源自拉丁语 dictatorius，来自 dictator（口述命令的人），dictator 来自 dictare（反复说），dictare 又来自 dicere（说）。

items.en: Dicere meant to say.
items.cn: dicere 意为说。

items.en: Dictare meant to say repeatedly or prescribe.
items.cn: dictare 意为反复说、规定。

items.en: Dictator named one who dictates orders.
items.cn: dictator 指口述命令的人。

items.en: Dictatorius meant belonging to a dictator.
items.cn: dictatorius 意为属于独裁官的。

items.en: Dictatorial entered English for absolute rule.
items.cn: 十六世纪 dictatorial 以绝对统治义进入英语。

items.en: It now also describes a bossy manner.
items.cn: 如今它也描述专横的态度。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dict- say family; the near-meaning group names other words for overbearing rule.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dict-（说）家族；近义组是其他表示「专横统治」的词。

entries.definition: A ruler with total power; the noun behind this adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 掌握全部权力的统治者；是这个形容词背后的名词。

entries.definition: Government by a dictator.
entries.definitionCN: 独裁者统治的政体。

entries.definition: To say orders or words for others to follow or write.
entries.definitionCN: 口述命令或文字让别人执行或记录。

entries.definition: Favouring strict obedience to authority.
entries.definitionCN: 主张严格服从权威。

entries.definition: Ruling with unlimited personal power.
entries.definitionCN: 以无限的个人权力统治。

entries.definition: Trying to control others without regard for their feelings.
entries.definitionCN: 试图控制他人而不顾其感受。

normalIntro.en: Dictatorial is dict- say plus -atorial: one voice says everything and no one else may answer.
normalIntro.cn: dictatorial 就是 dict-（说）加 -atorial：一个声音说了一切，别人不许回话。

normal.en: Dict- means say, as in predict.
normal.cn: dict- 意为说，如 predict。

normal.en: Dictator is the person, dictatorial the manner.
normal.cn: dictator 是人，dictatorial 是作风。

normal.en: It can describe a boss, not just a ruler.
normal.cn: 它可以形容上司，不只是统治者。

normal.en: Dictatorially is the adverb.
normal.cn: dictatorially 是副词。

normal.en: A dictatorial tone allows no reply.
normal.cn: dictatorial tone 不容回话。

abstract.en: One hand resting on every switch in a control room.
abstract.cn: 控制室里一只手按在所有开关上。

abstract.en: A plan slammed on a table while others stay silent.
abstract.cn: 一份方案被拍在桌上，其他人沉默。

abstract.en: A raised finger stopping a raised hand.
abstract.cn: 一根竖起的手指压住另一只举起的手。

examples.en: The regime grew more dictatorial each year.
examples.cn: 这个政权一年比一年独裁。

examples.en: He ran the kitchen in a dictatorial way.
examples.cn: 他以专断的方式管着厨房。

examples.en: Her dictatorial manner lost her the team.
examples.cn: 她专横的态度让她失去了团队。

dict_mnemonic.text: dictatorial ＝ dictator（独裁者，拉丁语 dictare「反复说、下令」，与 dictate、predict 同根 dicere「说」）＋ -ial（形容词后缀）＝一个人说了算的，「独裁的、专断的」。

root: 拉丁语 dicere（说）→ dictare（反复说、下令）→ dictator（独裁官）→ dictatorius → 英语 dictatorial

sensesIntro.en: One voice that silences others: a control room, a slammed plan and a raised finger.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个让别人闭嘴的声音：一间控制室、一份拍下的方案与一根竖起的手指。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand resting on every switch in a control room while the other chairs stay empty
core.cn: 核心意象：控制室里一只手按在所有开关上，其他椅子空着

branches.en: One hand resting on every switch in a control room.
branches.cn: 控制室里一只手按在所有开关上。

branches.en: A plan slammed on a table while others stay silent.
branches.cn: 一份方案被拍在桌上，其他人沉默。

branches.en: A raised finger stopping a raised hand.
branches.cn: 一根竖起的手指压住另一只举起的手。

branches.en: Both put all decisions in one hand.
branches.cn: 两者都把全部决定放在一只手里。

branches.en: Both leave no room for an answer.
branches.cn: 两者都不留回话的余地。

intro.en: Dictatorial is dict- plus -ator plus -ial; the say root also builds predict, contradict and verdict.
intro.cn: dictatorial 由 dict- 加 -ator 加 -ial 构成；说这个词根也造出 predict、contradict 与 verdict。

latinIntro.en: Latin dicere means to say, dictare to prescribe and verus true.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dicere 意为说，dictare 意为规定，verus 意为真实的。

definition_zh: n. 措辞；用语；吐字清晰度；表达风格
definition_en: the choice of words a writer or speaker uses, or the clearness of their speech sounds
core_image: 同一句话被改了三个词，语气立刻不同；播音员把每个字的辅音咬清楚
scene: 这首诗的措辞很朴素。The diction of the poem is plain.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：diction 指措辞、用语；句意是这首诗的措辞很朴素。

senses.title: Choice of words
senses.definition: the choice of words a writer or speaker uses
senses.definitionCN: 作者或说话者对词语的选择
senses.example: The diction of the poem is plain.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗的措辞很朴素。
senses.why: Three words swapped on a line of verse.
senses.whyCN: 一行诗里被换掉的三个词。

senses.title: Clarity of speech sounds
senses.definition: the clearness of the sounds when someone speaks or sings
senses.definitionCN: 说话或唱歌时发音的清晰程度
senses.example: The singer was praised for her diction.
senses.exampleCN: 这位歌手因吐字清晰而受称赞。
senses.why: A consonant marked sharply on a waveform.
senses.whyCN: 波形图上被咬得很清楚的一个辅音。

senses.title: A style of expression
senses.definition: a particular manner of expressing ideas in words
senses.definitionCN: 用文字表达思想的特定方式
senses.example: Legal diction differs from everyday speech.
senses.exampleCN: 法律用语不同于日常说话。
senses.why: Two columns of the same sentence in different registers.
senses.whyCN: 同一句话按两种语域排成的两栏。

intro.en: Diction comes from Latin dictio, a saying or manner of expression, from dicere, to say.
intro.cn: diction 源自拉丁语 dictio（说法、表达方式），来自 dicere（说）。

items.en: Dicere meant to say.
items.cn: dicere 意为说。

items.en: Dictio meant a saying or way of speaking.
items.cn: dictio 意为说法、说话方式。

items.en: Diction entered English for wording.
items.cn: 十五世纪 diction 以措辞义进入英语。

items.en: It also came to mean clarity of speech.
items.cn: 十八世纪它也指吐字清晰。

items.en: Diction is a standard term in literary study.
items.cn: 如今 diction 是文学研究的标准术语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dict- say family; the near-meaning group names other words for wording.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dict-（说）家族；近义组是其他表示「措辞」的词。

entries.definition: To say words for someone to write; it shares dicere but is a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 口述让人记录；共享 dicere，但是动词。

entries.definition: A book of words and meanings; it shares dicere through dictio.
entries.definitionCN: 词语与释义的书；经 dictio 共享 dicere。

entries.definition: A formal statement or saying.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的声明或格言。

entries.definition: The particular words used to say something.
entries.definitionCN: 用来表达某事的特定词语。

entries.definition: The way words are grouped into phrases.
entries.definitionCN: 把词组成短语的方式。

entries.definition: The set of words a person or language uses.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人或语言使用的词汇集合。

normalIntro.en: Diction is dict- say plus -ion: how the saying is done, which words and how clearly.
normalIntro.cn: diction 就是 dict-（说）加 -ion：说法是怎么完成的——用哪些词、说得多清楚。

normal.en: Dict- means say, as in dictate.
normal.cn: dict- 意为说，如 dictate。

normal.en: Diction is usually uncountable.
normal.cn: diction 通常不可数。

normal.en: Diction covers both words and clarity.
normal.cn: diction 既指用词也指吐字。

normal.en: Dictionary shares the same root.
normal.cn: dictionary 共享同一词根。

normal.en: Wording is the everyday synonym.
normal.cn: wording 是日常同义词。

abstract.en: Three words swapped on a line of verse.
abstract.cn: 一行诗里被换掉的三个词。

abstract.en: A consonant marked sharply on a waveform.
abstract.cn: 波形图上被咬得很清楚的一个辅音。

abstract.en: Two columns of the same sentence in different registers.
abstract.cn: 同一句话按两种语域排成的两栏。

examples.en: Her diction improved after the coaching.
examples.cn: 经过指导，她的吐字改善了。

examples.en: The essay uses formal diction throughout.
examples.cn: 这篇论文通篇使用正式用语。

examples.en: Different dictions mark different social groups.
examples.cn: 不同的用语风格标记不同社会群体。

dict_mnemonic.text: diction ＝ dict（说，拉丁语 dicere，与 dictate、predict 同根）＋ -ion（名词后缀）＝「说法」，即选哪些词、说得多清楚，「措辞、吐字」。

root: 拉丁语 dicere（说）→ dictio（说法、表达方式）→ 英语 diction

sensesIntro.en: One saying shaped: swapped words, a sharp consonant and two registers.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一次被塑形的说法：换掉的词、一个清晰的辅音与两种语域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three words swapped on a line of verse while the meaning stays and the tone changes
core.cn: 核心意象：一行诗里换掉三个词，意思不变而语气变了

branches.en: Three words swapped on a line of verse.
branches.cn: 一行诗里被换掉的三个词。

branches.en: A consonant marked sharply on a waveform.
branches.cn: 波形图上被咬得很清楚的一个辅音。

branches.en: Two columns of the same sentence in different registers.
branches.cn: 同一句话按两种语域排成的两栏。

branches.en: Both concern which words are chosen.
branches.cn: 两者都关乎选用哪些词。

branches.en: Both shape how a message lands.
branches.cn: 两者都塑造信息如何被接收。

intro.en: Diction is dict- plus -ion; the say root also builds dictate, dictionary and dictum.
intro.cn: diction 由 dict- 加 -ion 构成；说这个词根也造出 dictate、dictionary 与 dictum。

latinIntro.en: Latin dicere means to say, dictio a saying and verbum a word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dicere 意为说，dictio 意为说法，verbum 意为词。

definition_zh: adj. 说教的；教诲的；讲授式的；（贬）好为人师的
definition_en: intended to teach, especially a moral lesson, often in a way that feels preachy
core_image: 一本童书每页末尾都写着「这个故事告诉我们…」；老师把结论直接写在黑板上，不让学生自己推
scene: 这部小说太说教了。The novel is too didactic.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：didactic 指说教的；句意是这部小说太说教了。

pos.zh: 说教的；教诲的；好为人师的

senses.title: Meant to teach a lesson
senses.definition: intended to teach, especially a moral lesson
senses.definitionCN: 意在教导，尤指道德教训
senses.example: The novel is too didactic.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说太说教了。
senses.why: A moral printed at the foot of every page.
senses.whyCN: 每页页脚印着的一条教训。

senses.title: Teaching by telling
senses.definition: using direct instruction rather than discovery
senses.definitionCN: 用直接讲授而非让学生自己发现
senses.example: The method is didactic rather than exploratory.
senses.exampleCN: 这种方法是讲授式的，而非探索式的。
senses.why: A conclusion written on the board before the question.
senses.whyCN: 问题之前就先写在黑板上的结论。

senses.title: Preachy in manner
senses.definition: giving instruction when it is not wanted
senses.definitionCN: 在别人不需要时仍施以教导
senses.example: He has a didactic way of answering.
senses.exampleCN: 他回答时总带着说教腔。
senses.why: A finger pointing at a chart during a casual chat.
senses.whyCN: 闲聊中一根指着图表的手指。

intro.en: Didactic comes from Greek didaktikos, apt at teaching, from didaskein, to teach, built on an ancient root meaning to take or receive.
intro.cn: didactic 源自希腊语 didaktikos（善于教学的），来自 didaskein（教），其词根是古义的「接受、领受」。

items.en: Dak was the root meaning to take or receive.
items.cn: dak 是意为接受、领受的古词根。

items.en: Didaskein meant to teach, to make someone receive.
items.cn: didaskein 意为教，即让人领受。

items.en: Didaktikos meant apt at teaching.
items.cn: didaktikos 意为善于教学的。

items.en: Didactic entered English for instructive.
items.cn: 十七世纪 didactic 以教诲义进入英语。

items.en: It gained a negative preachy sense.
items.cn: 十九世纪获得贬义的说教色彩。

items.en: Didacticism names the tendency in art.
items.cn: 如今 didacticism 指艺术中的说教倾向。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the teach family across Greek and Latin; the near-meaning group names other words for instructive or preachy.
note.cn: 形近组共享希腊语与拉丁语的「教」家族；近义组是其他表示「教诲」或「说教」的词。

entries.definition: The tendency to teach morals in art.
entries.definitionCN: 在艺术中灌输道德的倾向。

entries.definition: Ready to be taught or led; it comes from Latin docere, to teach.
entries.definitionCN: 易受教、易引导的；来自拉丁语 docere（教）。

entries.definition: A follower who learns from a teacher; from Latin discere, to learn.
entries.definitionCN: 向老师学习的追随者；来自拉丁语 discere（学）。

entries.definition: Giving useful knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 提供有用知识的。

entries.definition: Giving moral advice in a tiresome way.
entries.definitionCN: 以令人厌烦的方式给道德劝告。

entries.definition: Intended to help people learn.
entries.definitionCN: 旨在帮助人们学习的。

normalIntro.en: Didactic is did- teach: the lesson is handed over, and sometimes handed over too hard.
normalIntro.cn: didactic 就是 did-（教）：把教训递过去，有时递得太用力。

normal.en: Did- here means teach, not do.
normal.cn: 这里的 did- 意为教，不是做。

normal.en: Didactic can be neutral or critical.
normal.cn: didactic 可中性也可带批评。

normal.en: Docile shares the teach root in Latin.
normal.cn: docile 在拉丁语里共享「教」词根。

normal.en: Didacticism is the noun for the habit.
normal.cn: didacticism 是这种习惯的名词。

normal.en: A didactic novel states its moral.
normal.cn: didactic novel 会直接说出教训。

abstract.en: A moral printed at the foot of every page.
abstract.cn: 每页页脚印着的一条教训。

abstract.en: A conclusion written on the board before the question.
abstract.cn: 问题之前就先写在黑板上的结论。

abstract.en: A finger pointing at a chart during a casual chat.
abstract.cn: 闲聊中一根指着图表的手指。

examples.en: The film is didactic but moving.
examples.cn: 这部电影说教却动人。

examples.en: She avoided a didactic tone in class.
examples.cn: 她在课堂上避免说教语气。

examples.en: His essays became more didactic with age.
examples.cn: 他的随笔随着年龄越发说教。

dict_mnemonic.text: didactic ＝ did（教，希腊语 didaskein「教」，本义「让人领受」）＋ -actic（…的）＝一心要把教训塞给你的，「说教的、教诲的」。与 docile、disciple 同出「接受」古根。

root: 希腊语 dak（接受、领受）→ didaskein（教）→ didaktikos（善于教学的）→ 英语 didactic

sensesIntro.en: One lesson handed over: a printed moral, a board conclusion and a pointing finger.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一份被递出的教训：印好的格言、黑板上的结论与一根指着图表的手指。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a moral printed at the foot of every page of a children book
core.cn: 核心意象：一本童书每页页脚都印着一条教训

branches.en: A moral printed at the foot of every page.
branches.cn: 每页页脚印着的一条教训。

branches.en: A conclusion written on the board before the question.
branches.cn: 问题之前就先写在黑板上的结论。

branches.en: A finger pointing at a chart during a casual chat.
branches.cn: 闲聊中一根指着图表的手指。

branches.en: Both give the answer before the thinking.
branches.cn: 两者都在思考之前给出答案。

branches.en: Both tell rather than invite.
branches.cn: 两者都是告知而非邀请。

intro.en: Didactic is did- teach plus -actic; the same ancient root gives Latin docere and discere.
intro.cn: didactic 由 did-（教）加 -actic 构成；同一古词根也给出拉丁语 docere 与 discere。

latinIntro.en: Latin docere means to teach, discere to learn and educare to bring up.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 docere 意为教，discere 意为学，educare 意为养育训练。

definition_zh: n. 柴油；柴油机；柴油车
definition_en: a heavy fuel oil, or an engine or vehicle that burns it by compressing air until the fuel ignites
core_image: 加油枪上标着更稠的一滴油；活塞把空气压到发烫，油雾一喷就自己烧起来
scene: 这辆车用柴油。This car runs on diesel.
sceneCN: 这里 diesel 是「柴油」这种燃料（第 1 个义项）；句意是这辆车用柴油。图中可辨识物件：加油枪、油滴标签、汽车油箱口。

forms.label: 复数（指柴油机或柴油车）

senses.title: The heavy fuel
senses.definition: a heavy oil fuel burned in compression-ignition engines
senses.definitionCN: （名词）在压燃式发动机里燃烧的重质油燃料
senses.example: This car runs on diesel.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆车用柴油。
senses.why: A pump nozzle labelled with a thicker, oilier drop.
senses.whyCN: 加油枪嘴上标着一滴更稠更油的油滴。

senses.title: The engine itself
senses.definition: an engine that ignites fuel by compressing air until it is hot enough
senses.definitionCN: 靠把空气压到足够热来点燃燃料的发动机
senses.example: The tractor has a four-cylinder diesel.
senses.exampleCN: 这台拖拉机装的是四缸柴油机。
senses.why: A piston squeezing air until the injected spray fires by itself.
senses.whyCN: 活塞压缩空气，直到喷入的油雾自行着火。

senses.title: A vehicle so powered
senses.definition: a car, lorry or locomotive driven by such an engine
senses.definitionCN: 由这种发动机驱动的汽车、卡车或机车
senses.example: The fleet replaced its diesels with electric vans.
senses.exampleCN: 车队把柴油车换成了电动货车。
senses.why: A lorry parked beside a charging van, keys on the same hook.
senses.whyCN: 一辆卡车停在充电货车旁，钥匙挂在同一个钩子上。

intro.en: Diesel is a surname: the German engineer Rudolf Diesel patented a compression-ignition engine, and his name spread to the engine and then to its fuel.
intro.cn: diesel 是一个姓氏：德国工程师鲁道夫·狄塞尔为压燃式发动机申请了专利，他的姓先成了发动机的名字，后来又指它的燃料。

items.en: Rudolf Diesel was a German engineer born in Paris.
items.cn: 鲁道夫·狄塞尔是生于巴黎的德国工程师。

items.en: He patented an engine that ignites fuel by compression alone.
items.cn: 他为一种仅靠压缩点燃燃料的发动机申请了专利。

items.en: A working engine was built and his surname became its name.
items.cn: 一台可用的发动机造出来了，他的姓成了它的名字。

items.en: Diesel then named the heavy oil such engines burn.
items.cn: 后来 diesel 也指这类发动机烧的重油。

items.en: Lorries, buses and ships adopted diesel power.
items.cn: 卡车、公交与船舶采用柴油动力。

items.en: Biodiesel blends plant-made fuel for the same engines.
items.cn: 生物柴油把植物制燃料掺给同样的发动机使用。

note.en: The look-alike group only shares the -sel spelling; the near-meaning group names rival fuels.
note.cn: 形近组只是共享 -sel 的拼写；近义组是与它竞争的燃料。

entries.definition: A stand for a painting; a spelling neighbour only.
entries.definitionCN: 画架；仅是拼写邻居。

entries.definition: A small long-bodied hunting animal.
entries.definitionCN: 一种身体细长的小型捕食动物。

entries.definition: A tiny piece of food.
entries.definitionCN: 一小口食物。

entries.definition: A light fuel ignited by a spark, the usual alternative.
entries.definitionCN: 由火花点燃的轻质燃料，是常见的替代。

entries.definition: The American word for petrol.
entries.definitionCN: petrol 的美式说法。

entries.definition: A medium oil burned in lamps and jet engines.
entries.definitionCN: 用于灯具与喷气发动机的中等油品。

normalIntro.en: Diesel is a man, not a root: remember the surname and the squeeze that lights the fuel.
normalIntro.cn: diesel 是人名不是词根：记住这个姓，以及那记点燃燃料的挤压。

normal.en: The engine is named after Rudolf Diesel.
normal.cn: 这种发动机以鲁道夫·狄塞尔命名。

normal.en: No spark plug: hot compressed air does the lighting.
normal.cn: 没有火花塞：靠被压热的空气点火。

normal.en: Diesel also names the thicker fuel itself.
normal.cn: diesel 也指那种更稠的燃料本身。

normal.en: A diesel can mean the whole lorry or locomotive.
normal.cn: a diesel 可以指整辆卡车或机车。

normal.en: Biodiesel is the plant-made cousin.
normal.cn: biodiesel 是植物制的表亲。

abstract.en: A pump nozzle labelled with a thicker, oilier drop.
abstract.cn: 加油枪嘴上标着一滴更稠更油的油滴。

abstract.en: A piston squeezing air until the injected spray fires by itself.
abstract.cn: 活塞压缩空气，直到喷入的油雾自行着火。

abstract.en: A lorry parked beside a charging van, keys on the same hook.
abstract.cn: 一辆卡车停在充电货车旁，钥匙挂在同一个钩子上。

examples.en: Diesel costs less than petrol here.
examples.cn: 这里柴油比汽油便宜。

examples.en: The generator uses a small diesel.
examples.cn: 这台发电机用一台小柴油机。

examples.en: Two diesels were shunting in the yard.
examples.cn: 两台柴油机车在调车场里调车。

dict_mnemonic.text: diesel 听着像「底子厚」——柴油比汽油稠，柴油机靠压到发烫的空气自己点火，底子厚才有劲。记住它是发明人狄塞尔的姓，不是词根拼出来的。

root: 德语姓氏 Diesel（工程师鲁道夫·狄塞尔）→ 1892 年专利的压燃式发动机 → 英语 diesel（柴油机／柴油）

sensesIntro.en: One squeeze that lights the fuel: a thick drop, a hot piston and a lorry key.
sensesIntro.cn: 一记挤压点燃燃料：一滴稠油、一个发烫的活塞与一把卡车钥匙。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a piston squeezing air until it glows hot and the sprayed oil catches without a spark
core.cn: 核心意象：活塞把空气压到发烫，喷入的油不用火花就自己烧起来

branches.en: A pump nozzle labelled with a thicker, oilier drop.
branches.cn: 加油枪嘴上标着一滴更稠更油的油滴。

branches.en: A piston squeezing air until the injected spray fires by itself.
branches.cn: 活塞压缩空气，直到喷入的油雾自行着火。

branches.en: A lorry parked beside a charging van, keys on the same hook.
branches.cn: 一辆卡车停在充电货车旁，钥匙挂在同一个钩子上。

branches.en: The engine is built around what this fuel needs.
branches.cn: 发动机是围绕这种燃料的需要造出来的。

branches.en: The engine name spreads to the whole vehicle.
branches.cn: 发动机的名字扩散到整辆车。

intro.en: Diesel itself is a surname, but the words around it are built from press-, ign-, petr- and bio-.
intro.cn: diesel 本身是姓氏，但它周围的词由 press-、ign-、petr- 与 bio- 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin ignis means fire, premere to press, oleum oil; Greek petra means rock.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ignis 意为火，premere 意为压，oleum 意为油；希腊语 petra 意为岩石。

definition_zh: 饮食；日常食物；节食；规定饮食
definition_en: the kind of food that a person or animal usually eats, or a limited plan of eating
core_image: 餐盘里一小块鱼、一把青菜、半杯水，旁边压着一张写满格子的纸
scene: 营养师把餐盘推回桌子中间，用笔敲了敲那张表格。Her diet is mostly rice, fish and green vegetables.
sceneCN: 这里 diet 指「日常饮食」（第 1 个义项：平时吃的东西）；句意是她的饮食主要是米饭、鱼和青菜。

senses.title: What one usually eats
senses.definition: the food and drink that a person or an animal normally takes
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或动物平时吃下喝下的东西
senses.example: A diet rich in fruit protects the heart.
senses.exampleCN: 多吃水果的饮食对心脏有保护作用。
senses.why: It is not one meal but the habit behind a hundred meals.
senses.whyCN: 它不算一顿饭，而是上百顿饭背后的那个习惯。

senses.title: Eating less on purpose
senses.definition: a limited plan of eating, usually followed to lose weight
senses.definitionCN: 为减轻体重而有意控制的一份饮食安排
senses.example: She went on a strict diet before the wedding.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼前她开始严格节食。
senses.why: A diet here is a rule set by the person against the person.
senses.whyCN: 这里的节食，是人给自己立下、又用来对付自己的规矩。

senses.title: A constant supply of the same thing
senses.definition: a long unbroken supply of something dull or unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 长时间不断涌来的一堆枯燥或难受的东西
senses.example: The audience was fed a diet of old songs and short jokes.
senses.exampleCN: 观众被迫听了一堆老歌和短笑话。
senses.why: The word lends the idea of feeding to things that are not food.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把「喂」的意思借给了并非食物的东西。

intro.en: Diet goes back to Greek diaita, a way of living, and reached English through Latin and French.
intro.cn: diet 可追到希腊语 diaita（生活方式），经拉丁语和法语进入英语。

items.en: Diaita meant a way of life, including food, exercise and sleep.
items.cn: diaita 指一种生活方式，包含饮食、运动与睡眠。

items.en: Latin diaeta kept the medical sense of a regulated life.
items.cn: 拉丁语 diaeta 保留了「有节制的生活」这层医学含义。

items.en: Diete arrived in French as the food a sick person should take.
items.cn: 法语 diete 指病人该吃的东西。

items.en: English diet first named a fixed allowance of food and drink.
items.cn: 英语 diet 最初指定量配给的饮食。

items.en: It split into the daily fare of anyone and a plan to lose weight.
items.cn: 它分成两层：人人日常的吃食，以及减肥的计划。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sound of diet, while the meaning group covers food supply, cooking and nutrition.
note.cn: 形近组与 diet 读音相近，近义组则覆盖食物供给、烹饪与营养。

entries.definition: a piece of music for two performers
entries.definitionCN: 供两个人演奏的乐曲

entries.definition: relating to what a person eats
entries.definitionCN: 与一个人所吃的东西有关的

entries.definition: a person who limits food to lose weight
entries.definitionCN: 为减肥而控制饮食的人

entries.definition: the process of getting the food a body needs
entries.definitionCN: 身体获取所需食物的过程

entries.definition: the food provided, especially at a meal or in a place
entries.definitionCN: 尤指一餐或某地提供的食物

entries.definition: the style of cooking of a country or a chef
entries.definitionCN: 一国或一位厨师的烹饪风格

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a plate of ordinary food and end with the word stretched to cover songs and jokes.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一盘平常饭菜开始，最后落到被拉去形容歌曲与笑话的那个词。

normal.en: Die with a t: die is what a strict diet tries to avoid.
normal.cn: die 后面加个 t：严格节食最怕的就是 die。

normal.en: A diet is not a meal, it is the pattern behind many meals.
normal.cn: diet 不是一顿饭，而是很多顿饭背后的模式。

normal.en: Go on a diet means the plan starts today, not tomorrow.
normal.cn: go on a diet 意思是计划从今天起，不是明天。

normal.en: A balanced diet needs colour on the plate, not just weight on the scale.
normal.cn: 均衡饮食要盘里有颜色，不能只盯着秤上的数字。

normal.en: A diet of bad news is still a diet, though nothing is eaten.
normal.cn: 满耳朵坏消息也叫一种饮食，虽然什么也没吃。

abstract.en: Picture a plate divided into small coloured sections.
abstract.cn: 想象一个盘子被分成几块颜色不同的区域。

abstract.en: Picture a chart on the fridge door with squares to tick.
abstract.cn: 想象冰箱门上贴着一张画满格子的表。

abstract.en: Picture a scale that moves only when nobody watches.
abstract.cn: 想象一台只在没人看时才动的秤。

examples.en: Poor diet is a leading cause of heart disease.
examples.cn: 不良饮食是心脏病的主要原因之一。

examples.en: He has been dieting since the spring.
examples.cn: 他从春天起就一直在节食。

examples.en: The children were given a steady diet of cartoons.
examples.cn: 孩子们被连续灌了一堆卡通片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 diet 记成「戴饿特」：戴着一份饿，特意少吃，就是节食。

root: 来自希腊语 diaita（生活方式），经拉丁语 diaeta 与古法语 diete 进入英语。本义是「有节制的生活」，尤其指病人该遵守的饮食安排；后来一方面泛指日常吃的东西，一方面专指为减轻体重而设的限制。

sensesIntro.en: From the food a body lives on, to a rule aimed at the waist, to a stream of non-food things forced down the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 从身体赖以活命的食物，到针对腰围立下的规矩，再到硬灌进脑子的一堆非食物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plate that is measured, not merely filled.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只被量过的盘子，而不只是被装满的盘子。

chain: THE SAME WORD FEEDS THE MIND

branches.en: The first sense is simply the pattern of daily food.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是日常食物的那个模式。

branches.en: The second sense adds a purpose: to become lighter.
branches.cn: 第二个义项添上目的：让自己变轻。

branches.en: The third sense feeds the mind instead of the body.
branches.cn: 第三个义项喂的是脑子，不是身体。

branches.en: The same plate serves health and vanity.
branches.cn: 同一只盘子，既为健康，也为体面。

branches.en: Both are about taking in less of something on purpose.
branches.cn: 两者都是有意少摄入某种东西。

intro.en: Diet builds a small family around eating, weighing and advising on food.
intro.cn: diet 围绕吃、称量与饮食建议，长出一小族词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Greek diaita through Latin diaeta, a way of living rather than a single meal.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是经拉丁语 diaeta 而来的希腊语 diaita，指生活方式而非一顿饭。

items.example: Her diet changed after the move.
items.exampleCN: 搬家之后她的饮食变了。

items.example: The doctor asked about his dietary habits.
items.exampleCN: 医生问了他的饮食习惯。

items.example: Most dieters give up within a month.
items.exampleCN: 大多数节食者一个月内就放弃了。

items.meaning: an expert in food and health
items.example: The dietitian wrote a simple weekly plan.
items.exampleCN: 营养师写了一份简单的周计划。

items.example: Constant dieting can harm the body.
items.exampleCN: 长期节食可能伤害身体。

items.example: She dieted for months before the race.
items.exampleCN: 比赛前她节食了好几个月。

items.example: Many diets promise more than they deliver.
items.exampleCN: 许多饮食方案承诺得多，兑现得少。
这家店卖适合控糖人群的糖。

definition_zh: adj. 饮食的；与饮食有关的；规定食物的 n.（旧）规定的伙食；食物配额
definition_en: relating to the food someone eats or to a prescribed eating plan; as an old noun, a fixed allowance of food
core_image: 食品包装背面那一栏「每份含量」；医院餐盘上一张写着忌口的卡片
scene: 包装上印着饮食信息。The label lists dietary information.
sceneCN: 这里 dietary 是「与饮食有关的」（第 1 个义项）；句意是包装标签上列出了饮食相关信息。图中可辨识物件：食品包装袋、成分表、每份含量栏。

pos.zh: 饮食的；与饮食有关的；规定食物的

senses.title: About what is eaten
senses.definition: relating to the food a person or group habitually eats
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）与一个人或群体习惯吃的食物有关
senses.example: The label lists dietary information.
senses.exampleCN: 包装上印着饮食信息。
senses.why: A food packet turned over to show the per-serving column.
senses.whyCN: 食品包装被翻过来，露出每份含量那一栏。

senses.title: Set by a health rule
senses.definition: required or limited by a medical or nutritional regimen
senses.definitionCN: 由医疗或营养方案规定或限制的
senses.example: She has strict dietary restrictions.
senses.exampleCN: 她有严格的饮食限制。
senses.why: A hospital tray with a card marking what must be left out.
senses.whyCN: 医院餐盘上放着一张卡片，标明哪些必须去掉。

senses.title: A fixed food allowance
senses.definition: a settled daily allowance of food in an institution
senses.definitionCN: （旧用法）机构中定好的每日食物配额
senses.example: The old workhouse kept a printed dietary.
senses.exampleCN: 那所旧济贫院保存着一份印好的伙食规定。
senses.why: A pinned sheet listing bread and gruel weights for each day.
senses.whyCN: 一张钉在墙上的纸，列着每天面包与粥的分量。

intro.en: Dietary comes through Latin diaeta from Greek diaita, a way of life; the suffix -ary turns it into an adjective about that regimen.
intro.cn: dietary 经拉丁语 diaeta 来自希腊语 diaita（生活方式）；后缀 -ary 把它变成关于这套规矩的形容词。

items.en: Diaita meant a way of life, not only food.
items.cn: diaita 意为生活方式，不只指食物。

items.en: Latin borrowed it as a regimen of living.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入后指生活的规矩。

items.en: Diaetarius described matters of that regimen.
items.cn: diaetarius 描述与这套规矩有关的事。

items.en: Dietary appeared as an adjective about diet.
items.cn: 十五世纪 dietary 作为关于饮食的形容词出现。

items.en: A dietary was the printed food allowance of a prison or workhouse.
items.cn: dietary 作名词指监狱或济贫院印好的伙食配额。

items.en: Food labels made dietary fibre an everyday phrase.
items.cn: 食品标签让「膳食纤维」成了日常说法。

note.en: The look-alike group is the diet- family; the near-meaning group names other words about food and nourishment.
note.cn: 形近组是 diet- 家族；近义组是其他关于食物与营养的词。

entries.definition: The food habitually eaten, or a restricted eating plan.
entries.definitionCN: 习惯吃的食物，或限制性的进食方案。

entries.definition: A specialist who plans diets for health.
entries.definitionCN: 为健康设计饮食的专业人员。

entries.definition: The science of diet and nutrition.
entries.definitionCN: 研究饮食与营养的学科。

entries.definition: Relating to the nutrients food provides.
entries.definitionCN: 与食物提供的营养素有关。

entries.definition: Concerned with nourishment and digestion.
entries.definitionCN: 与营养和消化有关。

entries.definition: A prescribed course of diet or exercise.
entries.definitionCN: 规定好的饮食或锻炼方案。

normalIntro.en: Dietary is diet plus -ary: anything about the diet, from a label column to a hospital card.
normalIntro.cn: dietary 就是 diet 加 -ary：凡是关于饮食的，从标签上的一栏到医院的一张卡片。

normal.en: Diet plus -ary means about the diet.
normal.cn: diet 加 -ary 就是「关于饮食的」。

normal.en: Dietary fibre is the plant part you cannot digest.
normal.cn: dietary fibre 是植物中你消化不了的部分。

normal.en: A dietary supplement adds what meals miss.
normal.cn: dietary supplement 补上饭菜缺的东西。

normal.en: Dietitian is the person, dietetics the subject.
normal.cn: dietitian 是人，dietetics 是学科。

normal.en: As an old noun a dietary was a printed food allowance.
normal.cn: 作旧名词时 dietary 指印好的伙食配额。

abstract.en: A food packet turned over to show the per-serving column.
abstract.cn: 食品包装被翻过来，露出每份含量那一栏。

abstract.en: A hospital tray with a card marking what must be left out.
abstract.cn: 医院餐盘上放着一张卡片，标明哪些必须去掉。

abstract.en: A pinned sheet listing bread and gruel weights for each day.
abstract.cn: 一张钉在墙上的纸，列着每天面包与粥的分量。

examples.en: Her dietary habits changed after the diagnosis.
examples.cn: 确诊后她的饮食习惯变了。

examples.en: The school meets all dietary requirements.
examples.cn: 学校满足所有饮食要求。

examples.en: The museum displays the workhouse dietary.
examples.cn: 博物馆展出那份济贫院伙食规定。

dict_mnemonic.text: dietary ＝ diet（饮食，源自希腊语 diaita「生活方式」）＋ -ary（与…有关的）＝「饮食的」；同族还有 dietitian（营养师）、dietetics（营养学）。旧时作名词指机构里印好的伙食配额。

root: 希腊语 diaita（生活方式）→ 拉丁语 diaeta（生活规矩、饮食）→ 中世纪拉丁语 diaetarius → 英语 dietary

sensesIntro.en: A way of life narrowed to a plate: a label column, a hospital card and a pinned allowance sheet.
sensesIntro.cn: 生活方式收窄到一只盘子：标签上的一栏、医院的一张卡片与钉着的配额表。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a food packet turned over so the per-serving column faces the reader
core.cn: 核心意象：食品包装被翻过来，让每份含量那一栏对着读者

branches.en: A food packet turned over to show the per-serving column.
branches.cn: 食品包装被翻过来，露出每份含量那一栏。

branches.en: A hospital tray with a card marking what must be left out.
branches.cn: 医院餐盘上放着一张卡片，标明哪些必须去掉。

branches.en: A pinned sheet listing bread and gruel weights for each day.
branches.cn: 一张钉在墙上的纸，列着每天面包与粥的分量。

branches.en: Both describe food through what a body needs.
branches.cn: 两者都从身体的需要来描述食物。

branches.en: Both turn eating into a written rule.
branches.cn: 两者都把吃饭变成写下来的规矩。

intro.en: Dietary is diet- plus -ary; the same field builds dietetics, nutritional and alimentary.
intro.cn: dietary 由 diet- 加 -ary 构成；同一领域还造出 dietetics、nutritional 与 alimentary。

latinIntro.en: Latin nutrire means to nourish, alimentum nourishment, fibra a thread and supplere to fill up.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nutrire 意为滋养，alimentum 意为食物，fibra 意为纤维，supplere 意为补足。

definition_zh: 不同；相异；意见不合
definition_en: to be unlike something else, or to hold a different opinion
core_image: 两条并排的路在远处分开，一条进林子，一条通向河边
scene: 两兄弟站在岔路口，一个指左，一个指右。Their opinions differ sharply on this question.
sceneCN: 这里 differ 指「意见不同」（第 2 个义项：看法不一致）；句意是在这个问题上他们的意见差别很大。

senses.title: To be unlike
senses.definition: to be unlike something else in one or more ways
senses.definitionCN: 在某一方面或几方面与别的东西不一样
senses.example: The two plans differ only in cost.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个方案只在成本上不同。
senses.why: Put two things side by side and a gap shows itself.
senses.whyCN: 把两样东西并排一放，缝隙自己就显出来了。

senses.title: To hold another opinion
senses.definition: to disagree with someone about what should be said or done
senses.definitionCN: 在说什么或做什么上与别人看法不一致
senses.example: Doctors differ about how much exercise is enough.
senses.exampleCN: 医生们对运动多少才算够看法不一。
senses.why: Two people can look at one fact and walk away with two stories.
senses.whyCN: 同一个人事实，两个人看完能带走两套说法。

intro.en: Differ comes from Latin differre, to carry apart, built from dis-, apart, and ferre, to carry.
intro.cn: differ 来自拉丁语 differre，本义是分开搬运，由 dis-（分开）与 ferre（搬、带）构成。

items.en: Ferre meant to carry or to bear a load.
items.cn: ferre 指搬运，也指承担一份重量。

items.en: Differre meant to carry things apart, and so to be unlike.
items.cn: differre 指把东西分开放，因而引申为不同。

items.en: The same verb also meant to put off until later.
items.cn: 同一个动词还表示把事情推到以后。

items.en: English differ took the sense of being unlike and of disagreeing.
items.cn: 英语 differ 承接了「相异」与「意见不合」两层意思。

items.en: The verb now anchors a whole family: difference, different, differentiate.
items.cn: 这个词如今撑起一整族词：difference、different、differentiate。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the diff- shape, while the meaning group covers varying, contrasting and deviating.
note.cn: 形近组共用 diff 这一形状，近义组则覆盖变化、对比与偏离。

entries.definition: to delay something to a later time
entries.definitionCN: 把某事推迟到以后

entries.definition: not the same as another thing
entries.definitionCN: 与另一事物不一样的

entries.definition: based on a difference between groups
entries.definitionCN: 基于群体之间差别的

entries.definition: to change or be different from one case to another
entries.definitionCN: 在个案之间变化或不同

entries.definition: to show a clear difference between two things
entries.definitionCN: 显出两物之间的明显差别

entries.definition: to move away from an expected path or rule
entries.definitionCN: 偏离预期的路线或规则

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with two roads splitting and end with two people reading one fact in two ways.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从两条路分开开始，最后落到两个人把一个事实读成两种。

normal.en: Dis- pulls apart, and ferre carries: differ is to carry apart.
normal.cn: dis- 往两边拉，ferre 是搬：differ 就是把东西搬开。

normal.en: Differ from names the other thing; differ in names the part.
normal.cn: differ from 接另一样东西，differ in 接具体方面。

normal.en: Two clocks differ by a minute and nobody notices for a year.
normal.cn: 两只钟差一分钟，一年都没人发现。

normal.en: To differ is not to fight, though a fight may follow.
normal.cn: differ 不等于争吵，虽然争吵可能跟着来。

normal.en: Different is the adjective, difference is the gap itself.
normal.cn: different 是形容词，difference 是那道缝本身。

abstract.en: Picture two roads leaving one field and never meeting again.
abstract.cn: 想象两条路从同一片田野出发，再没交汇。

abstract.en: Picture two rulers laid side by side, one a little longer.
abstract.cn: 想象两把尺子并排放着，其中一把略长。

abstract.en: Picture two hands pointing at opposite ends of a map.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手分别指着地图的两端。

examples.en: Their answers differ in almost every detail.
examples.cn: 他们的答案几乎每个细节都不同。

examples.en: Opinions differ on whether the plan will work.
examples.cn: 这个方案是否可行，意见并不一致。

examples.en: The twins differ only in the colour of their eyes.
examples.cn: 这对双胞胎只有眼睛的颜色不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 differ 记成「地分」：地一分两边，人就各站一边，于是不同、也不合。

root: 来自拉丁语 differre，由 dis-（分开）与 ferre（搬、带）组成，本义是把东西分开搬运。因为分开之后彼此不再相同，就生出「相异」；又因为各人把话带向不同方向，就生出「意见不合」。同源的 defer 保留了「推后」的古义。

sensesIntro.en: From two things carrying apart, to two minds carrying one question in different directions.
sensesIntro.cn: 从两样东西被搬向两边，到两颗心把同一个问题带向不同方向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two paths that leave the same point and never rejoin.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条路从同一点出发，再没有并回。

chain: TWO MINDS READ THE SAME FACT

branches.en: The first sense is about objects and the gap between them.
branches.cn: 第一个义项说的是东西本身以及它们之间的缝。

branches.en: The second sense moves the gap into people and their views.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把这道缝挪到人以及人的看法里。

branches.en: In both cases something is measured against something else.
branches.cn: 两种情形里，都是拿一样东西去比另一样。

branches.en: Disagreement needs no anger; it only needs two positions.
branches.cn: 分歧不必带火气，只要有两个位置就够了。

branches.en: A difference in facts often turns into a difference in judgment.
branches.cn: 事实上的差别，常常就变成判断上的差别。

intro.en: Differ anchors a large family built on the Latin stem fer-, to carry.
intro.cn: differ 撑起一大族词，词干 fer- 在拉丁语里是「搬、带」。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin ferre, to carry, with dis- meaning apart.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 ferre（搬、带），前缀 dis- 表示分开。

items.meaning: to carry apart, hence to be unlike
items.example: The two versions differ in tone.
The difference is small but real.
Every child learns in a different way.
items.exampleCN: 每个孩子学习的方式都不同。

items.example: He treats his two sons differently.
items.exampleCN: 他对两个儿子的方式不一样。

items.example: A child cannot differentiate the two sounds.

items.exampleCN: 细胞分化要经过许多步骤。

items.example: She was indifferent to the result.
His indifference hurt her more than anger.
items.exampleCN: 他的冷淡比发火更伤她。

definition_zh: 差别；差异；分歧；差额
definition_en: the way in which two people or things are not the same
core_image: 两只几乎一样的手套并排放在桌上，其中一只食指处磨破了一小块
scene: 店主把两只手套摊在柜台上，让顾客自己找不同。The difference between the two coats is only in the lining.
sceneCN: 这里 difference 指「差别」（第 1 个义项：不一样的地方）；句意是这两件外套的区别只在衬里。

senses.title: The gap between two things
senses.definition: the way in which two people or things are unlike each other
senses.definitionCN: 两个人或两样东西彼此不一样的地方
senses.example: The only difference is the size of the box.
senses.exampleCN: 唯一的差别是盒子的大小。
senses.why: Lay two things side by side and the eye finds the seam.
senses.whyCN: 把两样东西并排一放，眼睛就找到了那道缝。

senses.title: An effect that can be felt
senses.definition: the change that something brings to a situation or a life
senses.definitionCN: 某事物给局面或生活带来的改变
senses.example: One warm word can make a real difference.
senses.exampleCN: 一句暖心的话真能带来改变。
senses.why: Here the gap is not between objects but between before and after.
senses.whyCN: 这里的缝不在两样东西之间，而在之前与之后之间。

senses.title: A quarrel among people
senses.definition: a disagreement that keeps two sides apart
senses.definitionCN: 把双方隔开的那种不一致
senses.example: They settled their differences over dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在晚饭时解决了分歧。
senses.why: Two views pull apart until the people stand on different banks.
senses.whyCN: 两种看法越拉越开，人便站到了两岸。

intro.en: Difference comes from Latin differentia, built on differre, to carry apart, and entered English through French.
intro.cn: difference 来自拉丁语 differentia，词根是 differre（分开搬），经法语进入英语。

items.en: Ferre meant to carry, and dis- meant apart.
items.cn: ferre 指搬运，dis- 指分开。

items.en: Differentia named the quality that kept two things apart.
items.cn: differentia 指把两样东西区分开的那种性质。

items.en: Difference arrived as a word for a dispute as well as a gap.
items.cn: 法语 difference 既指缝隙，也指争执。

items.en: English kept both the physical gap and the quarrel.
items.cn: 英语同时保留了具体的差别与人和人的争吵。

items.en: The phrase make a difference grew into everyday praise for small acts.
items.cn: make a difference 逐渐成了对小事的日常褒奖。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the fer- ending, while the meaning group names gaps, marks and contrasts.
note.cn: 形近组共用 fer 结尾，近义组则分别指缝隙、标记与对照。

entries.definition: polite respect shown to another person
entries.definitionCN: 对别人表示的恭敬

entries.definition: not the same as another thing
entries.definitionCN: 与另一事物不一样的

entries.definition: based on a difference between groups
entries.definitionCN: 基于群体之间差别的

entries.definition: a clear difference between similar things
entries.definitionCN: 相似事物之间的清楚区别

entries.definition: an empty space or amount between two things
entries.definitionCN: 两物之间的空隙或差额

entries.definition: a difference made clear by putting things together
entries.definitionCN: 把事物放在一起而显出的差别

normalIntro.en: These hooks go from a worn fingertip on a glove to one warm sentence that changes a day.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从手套上一处磨破的指尖，走到一句能改变一天的话。

normal.en: Differ is the verb, difference is the thing you can point at.
normal.cn: differ 是动作，difference 是你能指出来的那个东西。

normal.en: Tell the difference means the eye has already done the work.
normal.cn: tell the difference 意思是眼睛已经分完了。

normal.en: Make a difference is a gap turned into a gift.
normal.cn: make a difference 是把一道缝变成一份礼物。

normal.en: A small difference in the lining can double the price.
normal.cn: 衬里上一处小差别，能把价钱翻一倍。

normal.en: Settle differences means the two banks join again.
normal.cn: settle differences 是让两岸重新接上。

abstract.en: Picture two gloves with one small worn spot between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手套之间只有一处磨破的小点。

abstract.en: Picture a thin line drawn between two almost equal circles.
abstract.cn: 想象两个几乎一样的圆之间画着一条细线。

abstract.en: Picture a door that opens because someone pushed it once.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门被谁推了一下，就开了。

examples.en: There is a big difference between knowing and doing.
examples.cn: 知道与做到之间有很大差别。

examples.en: A few kind words made all the difference.
examples.cn: 几句好话起了一切作用。

examples.en: The differences between the two reports puzzled the judge.
examples.cn: 两份报告之间的差异让法官困惑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 difference 记成「地分冷死」：地一分，两边就冷，差别与分歧都出来了。

root: 来自拉丁语 differentia，词根 differre 由 dis-（分开）与 ferre（搬）组成，本义是分开搬运。分开之后彼此不再一样，于是有了「差别」；各人把话带向不同方向，于是有了「分歧」。

sensesIntro.en: From a gap you can point at, to a change you can feel, to a quarrel that keeps two people apart.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一道能指出的缝，到一种能感到的改变，再到把两人隔开的一场争执。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin seam between two things that look almost the same.
core.cn: 核心意象：两样几乎一样的东西之间，那道细细的缝。

branches.en: The first sense is the visible gap itself.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是那道看得见的缝。

branches.en: The second sense turns the gap into an effect.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把这道缝变成一种作用。

branches.en: The third sense puts the gap between people.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把缝挪到人与人之间。

branches.en: A difference in things can harden into a difference in people.
branches.cn: 事物上的差异会硬化成人之间的隔阂。

branches.en: Settling a quarrel is itself a change that matters.
branches.cn: 解决争执本身就是一种要紧的改变。

intro.en: Difference belongs to the fer- family, all of it about carrying and being carried apart.
intro.cn: difference 属于 fer 一族，全都围绕搬与被搬开。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin ferre, to carry, with dis- meaning apart.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 ferre（搬、带），前缀 dis- 表示分开。

items.example: The difference is easy to see.
items.exampleCN: 这个差别很容易看出来。

items.example: We took a different road home.
items.exampleCN: 我们走了另一条路回家。

items.example: The second question was answered differently.
items.exampleCN: 第二个问题的回答方式不同。

items.example: Can you differentiate the two voices?
items.exampleCN: 你能分清这两个声音吗？
分化让每个细胞各有其职。

items.example: The crowd seemed indifferent to the speech.
items.exampleCN: 人群对那场演讲似乎毫不在意。
她的冷淡终结了那段友谊。

definition_zh: 区分；辨别；使不同；分化；求微分
definition_en: to recognize or make a difference between things, or to develop into a specialized form
core_image: 两件几乎相同的东西被一条细线分开
scene: 显微镜下，两张载玻片上的细胞看起来几乎一样。 Under the microscope the student differentiated the two kinds of cells that looked the same.
sceneCN: 这里 differentiate 是「区分、辨别」（第 1 个义项：看出两者的差异）；句意：显微镜下，学生区分开了两种看起来相同的细胞。

pos.zh: 区分；辨别；使不同；求微分

collocations.zh: 把 A 与 B 区分开

senses.title: Tell two things apart
senses.definition: to recognize that two things are not the same
senses.definitionCN: 看出两件事物并不相同
senses.example: Consumers cannot differentiate the two brands.
senses.exampleCN: 消费者无法区分这两个品牌。
senses.why: The Latin noun differentia means 'difference'. The verb's non-technical sense, recorded in 1876, is simply the mental act of drawing that difference.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 differentia 意为“差异”。1876 年记录的日常义，就是把这个差异在头脑里画出来。

senses.title: Make one thing distinct from another
senses.definition: to be the feature that makes two things distinguishable
senses.definitionCN: 成为让两物可被区别的特征
senses.example: Color differentiates the male from the female.
senses.exampleCN: 颜色把雄性与雌性区分开来。
senses.why: differre is 'to carry apart': dis- 'apart' plus ferre 'carry'. A feature that separates two things literally carries them away from each other.
senses.whyCN: differre 意为“分开携带”：dis-“分开”+ ferre“携带”。把两物分开的特征，字面上就是把它们各自带走。

senses.title: Develop into a specialized type
senses.definition: in biology, to develop from a general cell into a specialized one
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中，由普通细胞发育成专门细胞
senses.example: Cells differentiate into muscle, nerve, or bone.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞分化成肌肉、神经或骨骼细胞。
senses.why: The intransitive sense 'acquire a distinct and separate character' appeared in 1874. Biology took it literally: a cell takes on a separate identity.
senses.whyCN: 不及物义“获得独特而分离的性质”出现于 1874 年。生物学把它按字面使用：细胞获得了独立的身份。

senses.title: Make a product or brand different
senses.definition: to give a product a feature that sets it apart in a market
senses.definitionCN: 给产品一个在市场中被区别出来的特征
senses.example: The company differentiates its phones by camera quality.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司用相机质量让手机与众不同。
senses.why: Marketing extends 'make different' to competitive identity: the brand must be carried apart from every rival in the buyer's mind.
senses.whyCN: 市场营销把“使不同”扩展到竞争身份：品牌必须在买家心中与所有对手分开。

senses.title: Distinguish right from wrong
senses.definition: to draw a moral or conceptual line between categories
senses.definitionCN: 在类别之间划出道德或概念界线
senses.example: Children learn to differentiate right from wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子学会分辨是非。
senses.why: A judgment is a line between two categories. The same act that separates species or brands also separates acceptable from unacceptable.
senses.whyCN: 判断就是两个类别之间的一条线。区分物种或品牌的动作，也区分可接受与不可接受。

senses.title: Treat people differently
senses.definition: to apply different standards to people or groups
senses.definitionCN: 对人或者群体适用不同标准
senses.example: The law must not differentiate between rich and poor.
senses.exampleCN: 法律不得区别对待穷人与富人。
senses.why: When the line drawn between categories becomes unequal treatment, the verb takes a social and often negative sense. The difference stops being neutral.
senses.whyCN: 当类别之间画出的线变成不平等待遇，这个词就带上社会性、常为负面的含义。差异不再中立。

senses.title: Calculate a derivative
senses.definition: in mathematics, to find the derivative of a function
senses.definitionCN: 数学中，求一个函数的导数
senses.example: Differentiate the function with respect to x.
senses.exampleCN: 对该函数关于 x 求导。
senses.why: This is the word's first home: the 1816 mathematical sense. A derivative measures the rate at which a function changes, so the verb names the operation that extracts that rate.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最早的家：1816 年的数学义。导数衡量函数变化的速率，动词就指提取该速率的运算。

senses.title: Separate kinds in classification
senses.definition: to mark off species or types by their differences
senses.definitionCN: 按差异把物种或类型划开
senses.example: Taxonomists differentiate species by wing pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 分类学家按翅纹区分物种。
senses.why: Classification is literal marking-off, the oldest core of the word. Each category is a patch separated from its neighbours by a visible trait.
senses.whyCN: 分类就是字面上的“划开”，是这个词最古老的核心。每个类别都是被可见特征与邻居分开的一块。

senses.title: Differentiate oneself
senses.definition: to make yourself stand out from others by a distinct quality
senses.definitionCN: 以独特之处使自己与他人分开
senses.example: She differentiated herself through original research.
senses.exampleCN: 她以原创研究让自己脱颖而出。
senses.why: The reflexive form makes the person the object that is set apart. The line is now drawn between the self and the crowd, not between two external things.
senses.whyCN: 反身形式把人自己变成被划出的对象。这条线现在画在“自我”与人群之间，而不是两个外部事物之间。

intro.en: Differentiate was born in calculus and only later moved into ordinary judgment. Its parts are dis- 'apart' and ferre 'carry', the same verb behind transfer and refer.
intro.cn: differentiate 生于微积分，后来才进入日常判断。它的构件是 dis-“分开”与 ferre“携带”，后者也是 transfer、refer 的动词。

items.en: First recorded as a transitive verb in mathematics, 'obtain the differential coefficient of'.
items.cn: 最早记录为数学及物动词，义为“求出微分系数”。

items.en: From differentiatus, past participle of differentiare, from Latin differentia 'diversity, difference'.
items.cn: 来自中世纪拉丁语 differentiatus，即 differentiare 的过去分词，源头是拉丁语 differentia“差异、不同”。

items.en: differentia comes from differre 'to set apart', from dis- 'apart' + ferre 'to bear, carry' (PIE *bher- 'to carry').
items.cn: differentia 来自 differre“分开携带”，由 dis-“分开”+ ferre“承载、携带”构成（原始印欧语 *bher-“携带”）。

items.en: The intransitive sense 'acquire a distinct and separate character' appears, later central to biology.
items.cn: 不及物义“获得独特而分离的性质”出现，后来成为生物学的核心用法。

items.en: The non-technical transitive sense 'discriminate between by observing or describing the difference' is recorded.
items.cn: 非技术性的及物义“通过观察或描述差异来辨别”被记录。

note.en: The first group is about shared spelling and sound; the second is about verbs that also separate one thing from another.
note.cn: 第一组看共同的拼写与读音，第二组看同样把一物与另一物分开的动词。

entries.definition: to be unlike. It is the shorter verb behind difference and different.
entries.definitionCN: 不同；有差异。它是 difference 与 different 背后的短动词。

entries.definition: not the same. It is the adjective built on Latin differre.
entries.definitionCN: 不同的。它是建立在拉丁语 differre 上的形容词。

entries.definition: relating to a difference, especially in mathematics or mechanics.
entries.definitionCN: 与差异有关的，尤用于数学或机械。

entries.definition: to recognize or show a difference, often with careful attention. It is broader and more formal than differentiate.
entries.definitionCN: 认出或表明差异，常含仔细留意。它比 differentiate 更宽、更正式。

entries.definition: to perceive a difference, or to treat unfairly. The word carries a strong social sense that differentiate usually lacks.
entries.definitionCN: 察觉差异，或作不公平对待。它带有 differentiate 通常没有的强烈社会含义。

entries.definition: to move things apart or keep them apart. It stresses physical distance rather than perceived difference.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物分开或隔开。它强调物理距离，而非被感知的差异。

normalIntro.en: Real links: the Latin parts dis- + ferre, the 1816 calculus origin, biological differentiation, and the 1876 everyday sense.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁构件 dis- + ferre、1816 年的微积分来源、生物分化，以及 1876 年的日常义。

normal.en: differre is dis- 'apart' plus ferre 'carry': to differentiate is to carry two things apart in your mind.
normal.cn: differre 是 dis-“分开”+ ferre“携带”：differentiate 就是在头脑里把两物各自带走。
